---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-WASM-GATES-PASS-ON-A-MODULE-THAT-EXPORTS-NOTHING"
  title: "every wasm gate passes on a 368-byte module with no exported functions, so nothing would notice if the packaging never landed"
  epic: "ci-integrity"
  component: "CI"
  module: "wasm-gates"
  status: planned
  priority: high
  tracking_issue: 0
  dependencies:
    - "#1346 — the crate is not on the release train either"

  intent: |
    The crate's deliverable is a module a host can call. Measured today:

    ```
    $ cargo build --release --target wasm32-unknown-unknown      → ok          (gate: "release build for wasm")
    $ ls -l target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/rigorix_gate_wasm.wasm
      368 bytes                                                 ← no exported symbols
    $ grep -rc '#\[wasm_bindgen' src/                            → 1 match, inside a doc comment
    $ grep -c 'wasm-bindgen' wasm/Cargo.toml                     → 0
    ```

    All nine gates pass, including "release build for wasm". The build gate proves the crate **compiles**; nothing in
    CI loads the module, instantiates it, or calls `open_session` / `attempt_run` / `export_artifact_set` /
    `contract_version`. The Node harness that exists (`tests/host_verification/verify.mjs`) verifies a hand-written
    fixture artifact — it never touches the wasm build. So:

    - If the `#[wasm_bindgen]` layer never lands, **every gate stays green** and the crate still cannot be called.
    - The "bundle size" gate is in its `awaiting-packaging` state for the same reason: there is no artifact to measure
      (`measured_bytes: 0, budget_bytes: 0`), and it prints that honestly rather than pretending.
    - A 368-byte module passes the dependency-ban checks trivially — a tree with no exports links almost nothing, so
      "21 crates, no tokio/reqwest/libc" is a fact about a module that does nothing.

    This is the shape the crate's own gates were written to prevent elsewhere: a check that passes because it never
    had anything to check. The audit records it as "not implemented (4)" — but a not-implemented item inside a closed
    epic with 26/26 merged reads as done, and no gate would go red if it stayed that way forever.

  in_scope:
    - "A gate that loads the built wasm module and calls all four exported functions, failing on a missing export, an instantiation error, or a fifth function appearing unannounced — run in CI, in Node, against the release artifact rather than the source"
    - "A minimal assertion on each call: `contract_version` returns the three version numbers; `open_session` on a valid fixture returns a handle; `attempt_run` on the unlinked seam returns `kind: \"gate_unavailable\"` as `Ok`, not a throw; `export_artifact_set` before an attempt is a refusal"
    - "The bundle-size gate leaves `awaiting-packaging` only when that artifact exists, so the ceiling has a subject"
    - "The dependency-ban claim is stated against the shipped artifact, not a module with no exports"

  out_of_scope:
    - "The wasm-bindgen attribute layer itself, which is the packaging issue; this issue is the gate that fails until it lands"
    - "Publishing the npm package (#1346 covers train registration)"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "None"
    application:
      - "None"
    infrastructure:
      - "New: `wasm/ci/run-module-smoke.sh` (or equivalent) and its wiring in `run-wasm-gates.sh`; no library change"

  citations:
    - file: "wasm/ci/run-wasm-gates.sh"
      note: ":48 'release build for wasm' — the only gate that looks at the artifact, and it looks at compilation"
    - file: "wasm/ci/check-bundle-size.sh"
      note: ":74-83 the awaiting-packaging branch and its 'no exports yet' warning"
    - file: "wasm/src/interfaces/wasm_api.rs"
      note: ":17-19 the attribute layer deferred to the packaging issue"
    - file: "wasm/tests/host_verification/verify.mjs"
      note: "verifies a fixture artifact; never loads the module"

  verification:
    - "removing the wasm-bindgen attribute from one function fails the smoke gate, naming the missing export"
    - "a module that fails to instantiate fails the gate rather than skipping"
    - "the four calls behave as specified against today's unlinked seam"
---

# ISSUE-WASM-GATES-PASS-ON-A-MODULE-THAT-EXPORTS-NOTHING

## Measured

```
release cdylib            368 bytes
#[wasm_bindgen] in src/   0 (one mention, in a doc comment)
wasm-bindgen in Cargo     absent
run-wasm-gates            ✅ 9/9, including "release build for wasm"
anything that calls it    nothing
```

## Why this is the same defect class as everything else this quarter

A gate that passes because it never had a subject is indistinguishable from a gate that passes because the work is
right — until the day someone tries to call the module. Here the crate's own `check-bundle-size.sh` says it out loud
("no exports yet — not a shippable number"), and the size gate correctly refuses to enforce a ceiling; but the *build*
gate reports success, and the summary reads "wasm release build ✅".

The end state is one smoke gate that instantiates the artifact and calls four functions. It is cheap, it is the only
test that would notice if the crate were never callable, and it turns the size budget from a placeholder into a
measurement with an owner.
title: every wasm gate passes on a 368-byte module with no exported functions

---
guardian_issue:
  id: "ISSUE-COVERAGE-GATE-READS-REGIONS-AND-CALLS-THEM-LINES"
  title: "`coverage.sh --gate` extracts the first percentage of the TOTAL row — which is Regions — and prints it as line coverage; the per-layer thresholds it is compared to are ungated"
  epic: "ci-integrity"
  component: "CI"
  module: "coverage"
  status: planned
  priority: medium
  tracking_issue: 0
  dependencies: []

  intent: |
    `cargo llvm-cov --summary-only` orders its TOTAL row as
    `Regions · Missed Regions · Cover · Functions · … · Lines · Missed Lines · Cover · Branches …`, and the gate takes
    the **first** percentage on the last line:

    ```bash
    COVERAGE="$(echo "$SUMMARY" | tail -1 | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+%' | head -1 | sed 's/%//')"
    …
    echo "Line coverage: ${COVERAGE}% (threshold: ${COVERAGE_THRESHOLD}%)"
    ```

    Measured on this crate's application slice:

    ```
    TOTAL  251  26  89.64%  30  8  73.33%  169  11  93.49%  0  0  -
                    ^^^^^^ Regions                        ^^^^^^ Lines
    script reports : "Line coverage: 89.64%"
    actual lines   : 93.49%
    ```

    So the number the gate enforces and the number it prints are **region** coverage, labelled line coverage. The
    repository's own rule for this file is that the verdict comes from the line metric, and `--fail-under-lines`
    exists in the tool precisely so that extraction is not hand-rolled.

    Two consequences:

    1. **The workspace gate's threshold is applied to a different metric than its message names** — every green
       coverage stage printed a number that was not the one it claimed to check.
    2. **The three per-layer thresholds in the roadmap are compared to nothing.** Domain ≥95 %, application ≥90 %,
       interface ≥85 % are documented; the only gate is workspace-wide at 60 %. Measured here (lines, the metric the
       criteria are written against):

       | Layer | Criterion | Measured (lines) | Measured (regions) | Gated |
       |---|---|---|---|---|
       | Domain | ≥95 % | 91.62 % (49 of 585) | 89.52 % (77 of 735) | no |
       | Application | ≥90 % | **93.49 %** (11 of 169) | 89.64 % (26 of 251) | no |
       | Interface | ≥85 % | 74.47 % (84 of 329) | 75.68 % (117 of 481) | no |

       Note the application row: on the criterion's metric it **meets** the threshold (93.49 % ≥ 90 %), and only
       fails if regions are used — which is what the audit and the gate both did.

  in_scope:
    - "The gate takes its number from the Lines column, or delegates the verdict to `cargo llvm-cov … --fail-under-lines` and uses its exit status; the message names the metric it enforced"
    - "A self-test: a TOTAL row whose Regions and Lines differ must yield the Lines value, and a fabricated row with the columns swapped must not"
    - "The three per-layer thresholds are either gated (a per-slice measurement in CI, with the filter regexes the audit already uses) or removed from the roadmap; a documented threshold no gate reads is a criterion nobody enforces"
    - "The audit's three numbers are relabelled to the metric they were measured on (they are regions), and the application row's verdict is corrected to met-on-lines / unmet-on-regions with the metric stated"

  out_of_scope:
    - "Raising coverage; the question is which number is measured and whether anything acts on it"
    - "The wasm crate's own thresholds, except as the first consumer of a per-layer gate"

  affected_layers:
    domain:
      - "None"
    application:
      - "None"
    infrastructure:
      - "Modified: `.pi/scripts/coverage.sh` (extraction or delegation + self-test); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` if a per-layer gate is added"

  citations:
    - file: ".pi/scripts/coverage.sh"
      note: ":53-56 the TOTAL-row extraction; :69 the gate comparison"
    - file: ".github/workflows/ci.yml"
      note: ":174-175 'Workspace coverage (gated at 60%, baseline 78.92%)'"
    - file: "wasm/.pi/architecture/implementation-roadmap.md"
      note: ":188, :289, :341 the three per-layer thresholds and their measured values"

  verification:
    - "a TOTAL row with Regions 89.64 % and Lines 93.49 % yields 93.49"
    - "the printed message names Lines, and the gate's exit status matches `--fail-under-lines`"
    - "each per-layer threshold is either enforced by a CI job that fails below it, or absent from the roadmap"

# ISSUE-COVERAGE-GATE-READS-REGIONS-AND-CALLS-THEM-LINES

## Measured

```
TOTAL  251  26  89.64%  …  169  11  93.49%  0 0 -
script extracts "89.64%" and prints "Line coverage: 89.64%"
actual line coverage: 93.49%
```

## Why it matters twice

The label is wrong, and the mislabel propagated: the wasm audit reported its three coverage numbers from the same
column, so one criterion was marked unmet that meets its stated threshold (application, 93.49 % ≥ 90 %) and the other
two were described in a metric they were not measured in. A number is only a check when the reader can compare it to
the number it should be — and here the reader is comparing a region percentage with a line threshold, in a message that
says "Line coverage".

The second half is the governance gap: three documented thresholds, no gate that reads them. At 60 % workspace-wide,
the domain slice can fall from 91.62 % to 61 % and every build stays green.
title: coverage.sh --gate extracts the Regions column and prints it as line coverage; the per-layer thresholds are ungated
